findings.title: T2 (MA cross) is ahead so far, but the sample is tiny
findings.body: 6 alerts: 4 hit target, 0 hit stop, 2 still open. Three of the four wins are USDJPY buys in the same 9 Nov rally, so that is about two independent wins, not four.

findings.title: T1 (EDGE EXH confirmed) has the most alerts and the worst record
findings.body: 23 alerts: 3 hit target, 18 hit stop, 2 still open. All 15 stopped buys came on 16 to 19 Nov while the market was falling. Sells did much better: 3 target, 3 stop, 1 open.

findings.title: T3 (PC cross) has not won yet
findings.body: 10 alerts: 0 target, 5 stop, 3 open, 2 unclear. Buys were 4 stops out of 5.

findings.title: One market regime, so side may matter more than tier
findings.body: 6 to 20 Nov had a USD/JPY rally and then a sharp fall. Buys lost in the fall under every tier. With this sample the study cannot tell a good tier from a good market direction.

findings.title: T1 and T2/T3 are not scored the same way
findings.body: The 20 T1 alerts from 16 to 19 Nov are scored from the alert log: stopped if price touched the stop at any time before the opposite alert, with no time limit. T2 and T3 results were read by eye from the chart. T1 may look worse than it is.

findings.title: Compare each alert with the 4H trend at the time it fired
findings.body: Add the 4H trend (PEP, MA state, CVD) at alert time to every alert. Then compare with-trend and counter-trend alerts inside each tier. If with-trend alerts win far more in every tier, the trend filter is the edge, not the tier.

findings.title: Score every alert the same way
findings.body: For each alert record whether target or stop came first, and cap the holding time (about 5 days). Exact 1-minute data would help; it needs the TradingView Plus export.

method: Only confirmed 4H alerts are counted. T1 = EDGE EXH CONFIRMED. T2 = MA cross. T3 = PC cross. Sources: your Discord alerts (T2, T3, and 3 T1 sells from 9 to 10 Nov) and the TradingView alert log (20 T1 alerts, 16 to 19 Nov). Win rate = target / (target + stop), so open and unclear alerts are left out. Alerts from 11 to 15 Nov for T1 are not covered. The earlier label study is kept in study_edge.json but is not shown here.
